Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Adding a concrete draft for the Order Form exception block — copy below, happy to tweak wording: 

"Order Form Exception — Renewal Opt-Out and Delegated TFC:
1) Auto-Renew Opt-Out: Customer may elect to opt out of automatic renewal via the Redwood Console at least thirty (30) days prior to the renewal date. Redwood will maintain an auditable record of opt-out events linked to the Customer's account for a period of twelve (12) months.
2) Pilot Delegated Termination for Convenience: For pilot Order Forms (defined as Order Forms with committed term <= 180 days), Customer may designate in writing one (1) authorized business contact to exercise termination for convenience on behalf of Customer during the Order Form term only; such designation is non-transferable and expires at termination or expiration of the Order Form.

Notes on operational impact: Karthik: our Console already captures activity timestamps, but the 10-day window Susan requested is tight; 30 days is safer operationally to guarantee billing cycle alignment and to avoid proration disputes. If Acme insists on 10 days, we should require a documented billing cutover process and acceptance of potential prorations.

—Karthik
Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Team / Acme —

Legal has reviewed the proposed Order Form exception language and can accept a limited approach with the following modifications (summary):

1) Opt-out window: we prefer a thirty (30) day portal opt-out as Karthik suggested. If Acme requires a ten (10) day window, we can offer that as a one-time, escalated exception subject to a billing proration acknowledgement and a short written addendum signed by both parties.

2) TFC delegation: Acceptable for pilots only, provided language includes (a) explicit definition of pilot Order Forms (<=180 days, under $100k TCV), (b) non-transferability clause, (c) a mandatory notice requirement (written email from the designated contact to billing@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com), and (d) a limit of one delegation per Order Form. We recommend adding a sample designation template as an exhibit to the Order Form.

3) MSA carveouts: Confirm that the exception is expressly limited to the Order Form and does not amend the MSA; add a one-sentence cross-reference to preserve broader MSA termination rules.

Attached: redlines_legal_v2.pdf (legal redline with proposed edits inline).

If Acme signs to the one-time 10-day option, ask Procurement to include the proration acknowledgement in the PO and route the signed Order Form to DocuSign (link below). Otherwise, proceed with the standard 30-day portal opt-out and include the TFC exhibit.

Ben Carter
